title: Where is the edge in this row?
hook: To find an edge in a photo, must a computer first see what is bright and what is dark?

knows: a pixel row is a list of brightness numbers (light-adds-to-yellow)
doesNotKnow: that edges are where neighbouring pixels differ, found by sliding a tiny filter

misconception: An edge finder must recognise a bright or dark area first.
objective: The learner can explain that sliding a window that computes right neighbour minus left neighbour gives 0 on any flat patch, bright or dark, and a large value only where brightness changes: 200 200 200 10 10 10 gives 0, -190, -190, 0.

claims.text: For the row 200 200 200 10 10 10, right neighbour minus left neighbour at the four inner pixels gives 0, -190, -190, 0: two are not zero.
claims.source: Demo.tsx OUT_A via filt(); builder re-ran in Node (2026-10-14), matching the brief. Swapped row 10 10 10 200 200 200 gives 0, 190, 190, 0. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): VERIFIED. Own arithmetic on 200 200 200 10 10 10, right minus left at pixels 2-5: 0, -190, -190, 0 (two nonzero); swapped row gives 0, 190, 190, 0. Demo filt(row, p) = row[p] - row[p - 2] with 1-based p is right minus left.

claims.text: A flat patch gives zero whatever its brightness; only a change gives a nonzero value, and swapping bright and dark flips its sign.
claims.source: If row[p-1] = row[p+1] the difference is 0 for any common value; reversing the step negates row[p+1] - row[p-1]. Brief's further check: 0 0 0 9 9 9 gives 0, 9, 9, 0. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): VERIFIED. Equal neighbours give 0 for any value; reversing the step negates the difference (re-derived).

claims.text: Sliding a tiny filter like [−1 0 +1] along every row of a photo is a convolution, a basic building block of image processing.
claims.source: Strictly, sliding the window without flipping it is correlation; convolution flips the kernel, which for [-1 0 +1] only changes the sign. Image-processing texts and CNN literature call both convolution. Gonzalez and Woods, Digital Image Processing, spatial filtering chapter (ch. 3) (check before verifying). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): VERIFIED. Gonzalez and Woods not opened (cited from memory; no copy reachable). Verified on my own derivation plus web-search snippets (MathWorks 'Compare image filtering using correlation and convolution'; DIP course notes): sliding the window unflipped is correlation; convolution rotates the kernel 180 degrees, so this operation is convolution with [+1 0 -1], and image-processing and CNN usage call such sliding filters convolutions. The sentence is fair under that usage. Optional wording the builder could take: 'a convolution-style filter'.

recall.question: A pixel row reads 50 50 50 50 50 50. You slide 'right neighbour minus left neighbour' along it. What do you get at the inner pixels?
recall.why: Every window sees equal neighbours, so every difference is 0. A filter like this answers only to change, not to how bright the patch is.
